newsitem.title: USA: New England Power Pool warns of voltage reduction.
newsitem.headline: New England Power Pool warns of voltage reduction.

text.p: Operator of the New England power grid warned Thursday the region's utilities may need to reduce system voltage due to continued strain on generation resources from hot weather and high power demand.
Under its "Power Watch" advisory, New England utilities may have to reduce voltage or implement other measures to safeguard the six-state region's electricity system.
As of 1029 EST, the New England Power Pool's (NEPOOL) power load was 19,689 megawatts (MW).
The pool projected today's demand to peak at 20,450 MW with surplus generation on reserve at only 740 MW.
On Monday, NEPOOL reached a record peak load on its system of 20,534 MW.
NEPOOL also urged regional customers to continue to conserve energy.

The pool hoped to save up to 600 MW of power through conservation measures so it would not have to switch on old power plants which emit more air pollutants and in turn violate state and federal environmental air standards.
